find: return tieBreak(world, subject, a) > tieBreak(world, subject, b);
why: Rule 3 by name: equivalent candidates must be separated by a seeded PER-AI draw, never by slot or array order. Falling back to id order is precisely the bias issue #359 exists to remove, and with one player -- the campaign and the whole golden trace -- it is invisible, so only the symmetric multi-player fixtures catch it. Replaces ai-opponent-selection-reverses-slot-order, removed with issue #359: that entry mutated first-alive-in-array-order selection, which no longer exists, so its find string could only ever report failed-to-apply.
killedBy: committed opponent selection breaks a symmetric tie per-AI, rather than by slot order or in unison
committed opponent selection gives the same AI the same tie result every time it is asked
resolveOpponent: the one place an AI decides who it is fighting (issue #359) two AIs at the same spot no longer converge on one player by construction
